record.body:
**The icon thread from your screenshot — found it, and it is our own bug.**

The inactive icon has a vanilla fallback for the window before the custom texture dictionary is resident. That fallback was **`BLIP_CAMPFIRE` — the active glyph**. So an inactive campsite literally advertised itself as active until the dictionary loaded. That is exactly "now the inactive campfires are using the active campfire icon".

Two fixes:

1. **The fallback no longer lies.** It is now `BLIP_CAMP`, a distinct vanilla glyph attested in the Story scripts that does not depict a lit fire. A not-yet-loaded icon can no longer be mistaken for the activated state.

2. **The repair is no longer edge-triggered.** The recovery that swaps in the real inactive icon only ran on the single not-ready → ready transition. Any blip created or re-presented *after* that moment — placing a campsite, or a site re-shown after fast travel — never got a second chance and kept the wrong glyph for the rest of the session. Each blip now tracks whether it is wearing the fallback, so every stranded marker is repaired as soon as the dictionary is resident, and a correct one costs no native call. Eviction is handled too: if the dictionary is dropped, the markers are flagged for repair instead of being assumed correct.

This also explains the sequence you described. You saw the active icon on an inactive site (fallback, wrong glyph), then teleported away and back and got the inactive icon — because the round trip happened to re-present the blip after the dictionary had loaded.

The log now reports `inactive-icon fallback repaired sites=N dictionaryReady=1` when it fixes any, so this is visible rather than assumed.

**Unchanged and still open:** the activation problem. Your session showed `refs=0` on every presence line — `player_camp` not referenced — so an activation cannot commit even when correctly requested. The prompt-visibility instrumentation from my last comment is what settles whether the prompt appears at all. Staying `actionable` for that reason, not for the icon.

When you next load: check an inactive campsite shows the blacked-out flame icon rather than a lit one, then place a new campsite and confirm its icon is right immediately rather than only after travelling away and back.
